obligation.oracle: Every onboarded source contract MUST be versioned and validated; mutating operations MUST be correlated, deduplicated, reconcilable, retry-bounded, and safe under duplicate, delayed, partial, conflicting, and uncertain outcomes.

conventions.note: Every subject is tenant-scoped: the second token is the tenant id, mirroring the AsyncAPI channel addresses governance.{tenantId}.<domain>.<eventName>. A stream's subject filters therefore isolate one tenant's namespace and MUST NOT capture a bare cross-tenant wildcard at the tenant position.

streams.name: GOVERNANCE_EVENTS
streams.description: Tenant-scoped durable governance domain events. Publish-side mirror of the transactional outbox (0004_delivery.outbox_message): every mutating governance effect is published here exactly once per (tenant, dedup_key).

retention.discardReason: discard:new refuses NEW writes once a configured limit is reached rather than silently dropping the OLDEST retained events — data loss is fail-visible (a publish is rejected and surfaced) instead of a silent eviction that would make source history unreconstructable.
retention.maxAgeReason: maxAge is intentionally unset (null). Retention duration is NOT invented here; it is resolved from the longest applicable approved organizational/contractual/regulatory retention schedule and any active legal hold (research.md Decision 9). A concrete value is injected at deploy time from that resolved schedule; a hard-coded age here would silently override governed retention.

streams.replicasReason: R>=3 gives quorum durability so a single node loss does not lose committed governance events (safe under partial/uncertain outcomes).
streams.duplicateWindowReason: JetStream transport-level dedup on the per-message Nats-Msg-Id (the outbox dedup_key). A duplicate publish inside the window is deduplicated by the broker; application idempotency (0003_idempotency ledger) remains authoritative beyond the window. Deduplicated under duplicate/delayed redelivery.
streams.tamperEvidenceReason: denyDelete + denyPurge make the stream append-only from clients: retained governance events cannot be individually deleted or the stream purged, so source history remains reconstructable and tamper-evident.

ordering.note: Per-subject (per-aggregate) publish order is preserved by the outbox ordering_key mapped to the subject; JetStream assigns a monotonic stream sequence so out-of-order arrival is reconciled by sequence, never by wall-clock.

streams.name: GOVERNANCE_DLQ
streams.description: Tenant-scoped dead-letter stream. Receives events whose consumer redelivery budget (maxDeliver) is exhausted or that terminally fail processing. Mirrors 0004_delivery.dead_letter_record: retains the ORIGINAL message evidence before any transformation/replay, with paired replay authorization.

retention.discardReason: Dead letters are evidence; discard:new refuses to silently evict the oldest failed-message evidence.
retention.maxAgeReason: Dead-letter retention is resolved from the governed evidence-retention schedule (research.md Decision 9), never invented here.

streams.tamperEvidenceReason: Dead-letter evidence is append-only and tamper-evident; a failed message's original payload cannot be deleted or purged before human reconciliation.

consumers.name: governance-inventory-projector
consumers.deliverPolicyReason: deliver:all is replayable from the beginning — the correlated governance projection can be rebuilt deterministically (reconcilable).
consumers.maxDeliverReason: Bounded redelivery budget mirrors outbox/inbox max_attempts (default 8) in 0004_delivery — retry is bounded; the 9th failure is dead-lettered, never retried forever.

deadLetter.reason: On maxDeliver exhaustion the ORIGINAL message (payload + correlation_id + headers) is routed to the tenant's dead-letter subject and captured in GOVERNANCE_DLQ / dead_letter_record before any transformation, with replay authorization required to re-drive it.

consumers.name: governance-deadletter-triage
consumers.deliverPolicyReason: Dead-letter triage replays every retained failed message so an owner can reconcile it; no auto-drop.
consumers.maxDeliverReason: Dead letters are NOT auto-retried (maxDeliver:1). A human/owned triage flow reconciles them; unsafe automatic re-drive is blocked, and there is no onward dead-letter (a DLQ has no DLQ).

deadLetter.reason: The dead-letter stream is terminal; exhausted triage stays visible and owned rather than being routed onward.

deadLetterRouting.trigger: consumer maxDeliver exhausted OR terminal processing failure
deadLetterRouting.note: Every domain consumer routes exhausted redeliveries to the tenant's deadletter subject, captured durably in GOVERNANCE_DLQ. This mirrors the dead_letter_record table (origin, origin_message_id, correlation_id, original evidence, paired replay authorization) so a failed mutating operation is neither lost nor silently retried: it becomes an owned, reconcilable, tamper-evident record.
